coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 45–55 min Z2, rolling terrain if available, no fixed pace target. You're 12 days out in taper with a recovery score of 89 and resting HR 9 bpm below your 30-day average—your system is primed. This is a shakeout day to keep legs loose and turnover sharp without accumulating fatigue; your last three runs averaged 136–138 bpm, which is solid Build 2 work, but today drop to 125–130 bpm and focus on cadence and fluidity over effort. The Julian Alps is all about managing gravity and technical footing, not pace—use this run to dial in your downhill braking and ankle proprioception on uneven ground.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Post-run, prioritize 30–40g protein + 60–90g carbs within 90 min to anchor glycogen and muscle protein synthesis; your sleep efficiency is 93.9% and HRV data is absent, so this window is non-negotiable. Today's easy effort won't deplete you heavily, but taper is when many athletes under-fuel out of misplaced caution—don't. At race day you'll burn 4,000–5,500 kcal depending on effort and altitude; your fueling strategy during the race (bottles, gels, real food at aid) must be tested, but today and the next 11 days, eat to your training load, not below it.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: You logged 8.01 hours at 93.9% efficiency last night—that's elite-tier sleep for a 40-something exec on a travel schedule. Hold it. No sleeping pills, no late work emails; aim for 8–9 hours nightly until race day. Your resting HR is visibly lower than baseline; combine that with 89/100 recovery score and you have zero excuse to add volume or intensity today. Ice bath or cold plunge optional (prefer post-hard sessions only); instead, walk 20–30 min, eat salt + carbs, and keep parasympathetic tone high. This is when you harvest the 12 weeks of Build work.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Twelve days is short enough that nervous energy is rising—channel it into logistics, not self-doubt. Confirm your pre-race meals (what you'll eat the day before, the morning of, during aid station windows), test your pack weight and hydration system on Tuesday or Wednesday with a 90-min hill run, and review the course elevation profile and aid station locations obsessively. The Julian Alps is remote and vertical; knowing where to conserve, where to push, and how long between water stations removes variables on race day. Your fitness is built; your job now is to show up healthy, sharp, and strategically prepared.
